sentence: A high CRP means there is inflammation or infection somewhere in the body, but not where or why, so doctors read it with symptoms and other tests.
note: LTO: high or rising CRP suggests acute infection or inflammation but does not identify location or cause

sentence: CRP stands for C-reactive protein, a protein that the liver makes.
note: MedlinePlus: CRP is a protein made by the liver

sentence: Its level in the blood rises when there is inflammation somewhere in the body.
note: LTO: CRP rises with inflammation

sentence: Infection and several other causes of inflammation can push the level up.
note: MedlinePlus: rises after tissue injury, infection or other inflammation | edited after second pass

sentence: Doctors usually request the test when they suspect an infection or inflammation, for example after surgery.
note: LTO: requested when acute inflammation is a risk (for example infection after surgery) or suspected from symptoms

sentence: It is also used to help assess long-term inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis and lupus.
note: LTO: requested to evaluate chronic inflammatory conditions, rheumatoid arthritis and lupus named

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK says no special preparation is needed for the test.
note: LTO: no test preparation needed; venous sample is the usual route (textbook) | edited after second pass

sentence: A high or rising CRP suggests that there is an acute infection or inflammation.
note: LTO/MedlinePlus: high or increasing CRP suggests acute infection or inflammation

sentence: It does not show where the inflammation is or which condition is causing it.
note: both: does not help identify location or condition

sentence: For that reason the test is not diagnostic on its own.
note: LTO: the test is not diagnostic

sentence: Berkshire and Surrey pathology services say a raised CRP is linked with infection, particularly but not only bacterial, and with inflammation.
note: LTO news piece: CRP not specific for bacterial infection, frequently elevated in a wide range of other conditions | edited after second pass

sentence: A small rise is hard to interpret by itself, so doctors consider it alongside the whole clinical picture.
note: StatPearls: marginal increases are difficult to interpret and should not be used as an isolated result

sentence: In long-term inflammatory conditions the test is often repeated to see whether treatment is working.
note: LTO: in chronic conditions high level can signal flare or that treatment is not working | edited after second pass

sentence: The cause of a high CRP cannot always be found.
note: MedlinePlus: cause of high CRP cannot always be determined

sentence: MedlinePlus lists cancer, heart attack, infection, inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and related diseases, and rheumatic fever among the conditions that can raise CRP.
note: MedlinePlus list of possible causes

sentence: Not every cause is an illness.
note: LTO lists physiological causes (see next sentence); phrasing is the author's

sentence: A Danish blood donor study found low-grade inflammation was more common in women using the combined contraceptive pill.
note: both state this | edited after second pass

sentence: Obesity is linked with low-grade inflammation and with higher CRP levels.
note: LTO: obesity linked to higher levels | edited after second pass

sentence: StatPearls describes smoking, diabetes and other long-term conditions as associated with low-grade inflammation that can raise CRP.
note: StatPearls (blended summary): obesity, smoking, metabolic syndrome, diabetes, insomnia associated with low-grade inflammation and elevated CRP; second pass to confirm

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK says CRP is used to assess how severe inflammation is and how well treatment is working.
note: LTO: to determine acute inflammatory condition or flare of chronic disease | edited after second pass

sentence: The doctor may then arrange further tests or treatment.
note: LTO: doctor may follow up with further testing and treatment

sentence: The test is often repeated to see whether treatment has been effective.
note: LTO: repeated to track progress; levels drop as inflammation subsides | edited after second pass

sentence: NHS laboratories often report CRP results within about a day, though timing depends on where the test is requested.
note: LTO: on average 7 working days, depending on tests requested | edited after second pass

sentence: A CRP result does not show urgency; the NHS says chest tightness or pain spreading to the arms, neck or jaw needs a 999 call straight away.
note: signposting sentence; 999 for chest pain from NHS heart-attack page; the rest is standard NHS signposting | edited after second pass

sentence: StatPearls notes that small CRP rises can occur without obvious widespread inflammation.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: StatPearls: mild CRP elevations may occur in the absence of overt systemic inflammation.

sentence: High-sensitivity CRP, or hs-CRP, is a separate and more sensitive version of the test.
note: LTO hs-CRP page: hs-CRP separate, more sensitive

sentence: It has been used to estimate the risk of heart disease in people who seem healthy.
note: LTO hs-CRP page

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK notes that current UK guidelines on cardiovascular risk assessment do not recommend hs-CRP testing.
note: LTO hs-CRP page

sentence: A Sheffield NHS laboratory leaflet says hs-CRP should not replace assessment of the usual cardiovascular risk factors.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: Sheffield says hsCRP should not be a substitute for assessment of traditional cardiovascular risk factors.

sentence: The same leaflet says people with active infection, inflammation or trauma should not have hs-CRP testing until these have resolved.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: Sheffield advises people with active infection, inflammation or trauma wait until settled before hsCRP-based CVD risk assessment.

sentence: StatPearls states that some medicines, including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and statins, can lower CRP.
note: StatPearls (blended summary): NSAIDs and statins can reduce CRP; second pass to confirm

sentence: Long-term conditions linked with low-grade inflammation can lift it.
note: same blended summary

sentence: Regional NHS guidance on suspected giant cell arteritis, an inflammation of blood vessels, asks for a CRP before steroids are started.
note: Devon formulary (blended summary): CRP taken before steroids; second pass to confirm

sentence: A Devon formulary page says polymyalgia rheumatica is possible but very rare when inflammatory markers are normal.
note: NHS 111 Wales (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: Scottish referral guidance for suspected rheumatoid arthritis refers to CRP and ESR results alongside anti-CCP and rheumatoid factor tests.
note: NHS Tayside guide (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: It advises referral for persistent symptoms even when CRP is normal and antibodies are negative.
note: same

sentence: A Scottish NHS guideline on giant cell arteritis says it is rare to see the condition with normal inflammatory markers, and that CRP, plasma viscosity or both should be raised.
note: added after second pass: third-pass supported: NHS Highland GCA page: rarely see GCA with normal inflammatory markers; CRP, PV or both should be raised.

sentence: A high CRP shows that inflammation or infection is likely, but it does not show where it is or what is causing it.
note: as above

sentence: CRP is a protein made by the liver whose level rises when there is inflammation in the body.
note: MedlinePlus: CRP is made by the liver; rises after injury, infection, other inflammation | edited after second pass

sentence: Doctors read the result with the wider clinical picture, and the test is often repeated to see whether treatment has worked.
note: LTO: used with signs, symptoms, exam and other tests; often repeated to track progress | edited after second pass

sentence: Some raised results are linked to things other than illness, such as obesity or taking the combined contraceptive pill.
note: both list pregnancy, contraceptive pill and HRT | edited after second pass

sentence: Laboratories and sources do not all use the same cut-offs, so a CRP result is read against the range on its own report.
note: LTO notes ranges vary by laboratory; NHS lab directory pages give their own ranges | edited after second pass
